title: Picovoice Pricing 2026: Free, Foundation & Enterprise
summary: Picovoice pricing includes three annual tiers: Free, Foundation ($6,000), and Enterprise ($30,000). There's no per-call billing.
body_markdown:
## Calling a Speech API from an Activepieces Workflow


Activepieces runs server-side transcription jobs as flows, with 747 integrations to connect the speech provider, storage and database around them.


It can send an audio file to a cloud speech API over HTTP, but it can't run Picovoice's on-device SDKs, which live inside the app on the phone.


### When to use speech in a workflow


A workflow runs on a server, on a trigger, with no microphone in the loop. That makes it a fit for recorded audio: voicemails, uploaded meeting files, call recordings.


Nobody is waiting on the result, so the latency that justified a streaming tier in the previous section doesn't apply, and batch transcription is the cheaper path to price.


On the other side of that line sits the Picovoice SDK. It processes audio inside the phone app, and a workflow never sees that audio unless your app uploads it.


If your plan was to drop the SDK into a flow, the plan fails at the first step.


If you want the on-device pricing and limits to apply, the speech has to stay in the app. If you want a workflow, you're buying a cloud API and its meter instead.


On the left is the app with the SDK, marked as running on the device and not in workflows; on the right, a separate server lane carries an audio file through an Activepieces flow to a cloud speech API, then to text, then to a database.


Take from it that these are two different cost models, and your bill depends on which lane the audio travels.


1. Start the flow when a file lands, whether by webhook from your app, a new object in storage, or a scheduled check of a folder.
2. Use the HTTP integration to send the audio to the speech provider's endpoint, with your key stored as a connection, not pasted into the step. Read the provider's pricing page for the metered unit first, since audio length and request count are billed differently.
3. Parse the returned text and keep the job or request ID, so a failed run can be retried without paying to transcribe the same file twice.
4. Write the text and the ID to your database.
5. End the flow by adding the audio length to a running total.


Those five steps are one run.


Activepieces's pricing page lists a run as 1 credit however many steps it has, whereas Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's pricing page bills per module, so the retry and bookkeeping steps cost nothing extra here and would add to the count there.


The free plan carries 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows. The transcription meter that matters is still the speech provider's, not the flow's.


### Setting usage alerts before the quota runs out


By step five, the headline plan stops being the whole story. Free tiers and entry plans cap usage, and a cap you discover by hitting it arrives as failed runs or an unplanned invoice.


Keep a counter of audio processed, compare it against the limit stated on the vendor's page, and have the flow send a message to your team when usage crosses a threshold you chose in advance.


Check the vendor's current limits when you set that threshold, because the number you copy today is the one that quietly goes stale.
